title: SSH is running on the default port (22)
description: Port 22 is the first target of the automated scanners and brute-force traffic on the internet. Moving SSH to another port removes almost all of it.
descriptionMixed: Port 22 is still open, alongside {{ports}}. Close 22 once the move is verified; the attack surface stays open until then.
step2: Tell SELinux about the new port. sshd does not start at all if this step is skipped:
step3: Open the new port and close 22 under
step4: Check the configuration and restart sshd:
step5: WITHOUT CLOSING THE CURRENT SSH SESSION, open a second session on the new port and confirm it works. Only then close port 22.
note: This warning disappears on its own once sshd no longer answers on 22.
